uncited: Hierarchical data structures accelerate volume rendering by organizing voxel data into a spatial subdivision hierarchy where internal nodes store aggregate information derived from their children or leaf voxels [Parent](4392-hierarchical-and-block-based-data-structures.md).

All methods in this family rely on a spatial subdivision hierarchy where internal nodes store aggregate information derived from their children or leaf voxels [Parent](4392-hierarchical-and-block-based-data-structures.md).
Internal nodes aggregate these properties (e.g., binary occupancy, min/max scalar ranges) from their children [Parent](4392-hierarchical-and-block-based-data-structures.md).

**Pruning:** During ray traversal, if a node indicates an empty or inactive region (e.g., occupancy flag is 0, or min/max bounds are outside the transfer function's opacity range), the entire subtree is skipped [Parent](4392-hierarchical-and-block-based-data-structures.md).
**Construction:** The hierarchy is typically constructed bottom-up [Parent](4392-hierarchical-and-block-based-data-structures.md).

The depth is determined by data dimensions, often requiring padding to powers of two or specific size constraints to maintain regular subdivision [Parent](4392-hierarchical-and-block-based-data-structures.md).
Early work focused on octrees and kd-trees to skip empty space [Parent](4392-hierarchical-and-block-based-data-structures.md).
